# v2.26-dev Release Notes

## New: Inactivity (idle) session timeout

Signed-in users are now automatically signed out after a period of inactivity,
instead of only ever being logged out at a fixed 8-hour mark.

### What's new

- **Idle timeout** — After a configurable period of no activity (default
  **30 minutes**), a user's session ends and they're returned to the login page.
- **"Still there?" warning** — About a minute before the timeout, a dialog with
  a live countdown appears so an active user can click **Stay signed in** and
  keep working. No more surprise sign-outs mid-task.
- **Stays alive while you work** — Ongoing activity keeps the session alive
  automatically; the timer only counts genuine inactivity.
- **Admin control** — SuperAdmins set the idle timeout under
  **Admin → System Settings → Session** (5 minutes to 24 hours).

### Unchanged

- A fixed **absolute cap** (8 hours) still applies — every session ends once it
  reaches the cap, even for a continuously-active user. This can be overridden
  per deployment with the `SESSION_ABSOLUTE_HOURS` environment variable.

### Notes

- Includes a small database migration adding the new setting
  (`session_idle_minutes`, default 30). It runs automatically on update.
- Existing signed-in sessions are unaffected until the user next signs in, at
  which point the new idle timeout applies.

No action needed after updating beyond the automatic migration.
